name: Memory Retrieval
summary: Every new perception is compared against a lifetime of stored experience.
description: The hippocampus acts as an index — it doesn't store memories itself but binds together the distributed cortical patterns that represent a memory. Semantic memory (facts and knowledge) provides conceptual frameworks. Episodic memory (personal experiences) adds autobiographical context. Memory retrieval isn't like reading a file — it's a reconstruction. Each time you remember something, the memory is rebuilt from fragments and can be subtly altered in the process. This is why eyewitness testimony is notoriously unreliable.
